name: Cantonese Assembly Hall
kicker: Cantonese hall with a pottery dragon
summary: The Cantonese merchants’ hall, built in 1885, with a pottery dragon fountain in the front court and a hall of carved wood and stone behind it. It began as a place for Thiên Hậu and Confucius; after 1911 the worship turned to Quan Công. A short stop on the old-town loop.
fee: 20,000 VND from 10 Aug 2026, or a combination ticket
getThere: Walk the old town; ask for Hội quán Quảng Đông
heroCaption: The pottery dragon in the court, with the gate behind it

notice.title: Look for the pottery dragon
notice.body: No door number is published. Ask for Hội quán Quảng Đông, the Cantonese hall with the dragon in the court, once you are on Trần Phú.

body: Cantonese merchants built the hall in 1885, first for Thiên Hậu and Confucius. After 1911 the worship turned to Quan Công and the founding merchants, the Tiền Hiền. A pottery dragon fountain fills the court. That is the frame you recognise before you reach the hall.

Inside are four large horizontal boards, a bronze censer 1.6 metres high and 0.6 metres wide, and a pair of Chinese celadon pedestals. The wood and stone structure is the point of the visit. The hall marks Nguyên tiêu on the 15th of the first lunar month and Quan Công’s day on the 24th of the sixth lunar month.
If you only enter one hall, the long Fujian hall on Trần Phú is the other choice. This one is the dragon court.

figures.caption: The hall behind the dragon
figures.alt: The tiled hall of the Cantonese Assembly Hall in Hoi An, with a ceramic dragon in front

gettingThere: The hall is in the old town. Walk from Trần Phú and ask for Hội quán Quảng Đông, the court with the pottery dragon.

legs.heading: From the old town
legs.body: Walk, and ask for the Cantonese hall once you are on Trần Phú.

admissionNote: No separate price for this building. From 10 Aug 2026: 20,000 VND per person per building, the same for every visitor (Da Nang Resolution 98/2026). Heritage centre notices of 26 Jan and 16 Mar 2026: 80,000 VND (streetscape, Chùa Cầu or Miếu Quan Công, and two other works) or 120,000 VND (adds a museum and three other works), usable through a stay of up to three days. A May 2026 article counts those as four and six works. Ask at the booth which ticket is on sale.
